standard_prerequisites.name: Detecting surjectivity on the relative cotangent space
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma that a map in the completed category is surjective exactly when its relative cotangent space vanishes
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the nonvanishing of the relative cotangent space when f is not surjective, hence the nonvanishing of the quotient Q.

standard_prerequisites.name: Structure of the quotient by the subring and the square of the maximal ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard properties of the quotient of a local algebra by the image of a ring map plus the square of its maximal ideal, making it a vector space over the residue field
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identification of Q as a k-vector space and as an S-module through the residue field.

core_obligations: Assume f is not surjective (proof lines 1226-1232): then the relative cotangent space m_S/(m_R S + m_S^2) is nonzero, and consequently the quotient Q = S/(f(R) + m_R S + m_S^2) is nonzero; Q becomes a k-vector space and an S-module via the residue map.

Show the quotient map is a derivation (proof lines 1232-1243): writing elements of S as images of elements of R plus elements of the maximal ideal, and using that the two summands have the same image in k, one computes a_1a_2 = f(b_1)a_2 + f(b_2)a_1 in Q, which is exactly the Leibniz rule, so the quotient map is a Lambda-derivation vanishing after composing with R -> S.

Conclude (proof lines 1243-1246): since Q is nonzero there also exist derivations S -> k vanishing on the image of R, so the restriction map Der_Lambda(S, k) -> Der_Lambda(R, k) is not injective, which is the contrapositive of the statement.
proof_roadmap: Translate nonsurjectivity into the nonvanishing of a relative cotangent quotient.
Verify the Leibniz rule for the quotient map by an explicit computation in that quotient.
Deduce the existence of a nonzero derivation trivial on R, contradicting injectivity.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a morphism in the completed category is surjective if the restriction of Lambda-derivations into k from the target to the source is injective (statement lines 1219-1224). The proof (proof lines 1226-1248) translates nonsurjectivity into the nonvanishing of a quotient, verifies by an explicit computation that the quotient map satisfies the Leibniz rule, and deduces a derivation trivial on the source. H2: a contrapositive argument with an explicit Leibniz computation, written out in full.
